the ask, verbatim
Produce ONE v2-format edition through the paper's full pipeline: three independent drafts, one selection, one adversarial review. The edition spec every draft must follow in full: Produce today's EDITION of Open Interest's daily crypto brief, format v2: a NEWSPAPER, not a research digest. Plain text only, under 1,700 words. Quality of news judgment, voice and sourcing is the entire point. FIRST: fetch and obey the house style guide at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/style-guide.html (binding: declarative sentences, numbers with context, banned words, at most one em dash PER STORY, absolute dates, no financial advice). Cite with the full source URL in square brackets. STRUCTURE - copy this skeleton verbatim. Section headers must appear character for character as written here, each at the start of its own line, colon included: "LEAD:", "NEWS:", "TECH:", "CULTURE:", "READING LIST:", "METHOD:". No other header form is accepted. You may open with the masthead banner (OPEN INTEREST / Daily brief, format v2. <Weekday>, <D Month YYYY>.) before LEAD:. LEAD: <the day's single most consequential story, ANY category - an exploit, a ruling, an upgrade, a collapse. Declarative headline ending in a full stop.> <two-sentence deck> <200-300 words, every claim sourced> NEWS: [NEWS] <declarative headline ending in a full stop.> <3-4 sentences, at least one source URL. EVENTS: hacks and exploits, regulation and enforcement, exchanges and companies, market-structure events. Never price commentary.> <exactly three [NEWS] items in all> TECH: [TECH] <same shape: protocols, research, engineering.> <exactly two [TECH] items in all> CULTURE: [CULTURE] <same shape: governance fights, community conflicts, narratives, the people and institutions of the discourse.> <exactly two [CULTURE] items in all> READING LIST: [https://<full url>] <one-line reason ending in a full stop.> <3-5 entries, one entry per line, URL in square brackets> METHOD: <one closing paragraph: sources swept, hours covered, items cut for failed verification, claims resting on secondary sources.> SOURCES - the roster and the record: - The paper's masthead (88 voices): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/masthead/voices.csv - prefer these voices' own writing for TECH and CULTURE. - ROTATION, binding: the roster holds 88 voices; the paper reads all of them, not its favourites. Under CONTINUITY you fetch the archive - note every voice and outlet the three most recent published editions cite. None of them may be cited again today, with ONE exception per edition: a repeat is allowed only when that voice or outlet is itself the subject of a news event, and the repeat is disclosed in METHOD. Draw today's TECH and CULTURE voices and the READING LIST from parts of the roster the archive has not yet quoted. - NEWS events may rest on: official announcements, status pages and company blogs; ON-CHAIN EVIDENCE and analytics investigations (cite transactions and addresses where material); court and regulator documents; and reputable secondary reporting ATTRIBUTED BY NAME where no primary source exists - never stated as bare fact, always disclosed in METHOD. - X only via open mirrors. Prefer the last 24-48 hours. - A claim that cannot be verified is cut, and the cut is noted in METHOD. When sources conflict on a figure, prefer the primary source; otherwise state the range and attribute both. CONTINUITY: before drafting, fetch https://openinterest.news/ (today's edition and the archive) and https://openinterest.news/rehearsal.html, and the prior editions linked there. Do NOT lead with a story a prior edition led with unless a material NEW development happened after it. ACCEPTANCE: the skeleton above complete, headers verbatim, with EXACT section counts; every claim sourced; under 1,700 words; no banned words; headlines are declarative sentences with full stops; absolute dates only; at most one em dash per story.
